messages.author: 4fe26caaac11aa72
messages.subject: muthen1984 - problems with exogenous predictors
parts:
Dear Yves, dear all,

I specify a model with three latent variables (lv1, lv2, and lv3), of which only the first uses dichotomous data.
In the prediction model I want to take into account two exogenous variables (sex and mig), that is, regress both the outcome and the other latent predictors on these two variables.
If you estimate such an model in Mplus (with specifying variance and covariances of the exogenous variables) the exogenous variables are transposed to latent variables, that is the reason why I specified the following model:

dat <- read.csv("c:/../short.csv")
psych::describe(dat)
mod <- paste("lv1 =~ lv1_i01 + lv1_i02 + lv1_i03 + lv1_i04 + lv1_i05
      lv2 =~ lv2_i01 + lv2_i02 + lv2_i03 + lv2_i04 
              lv3 =~ lv3_i01 + lv3_i02 + lv3_i03 + lv3_i04
      # specify pseudo-latent variables for exogenous variables
      sex =~ sex.orig
      mig =~ mig.orig
      # specify regressions
      outcome ~ sex + mig + lv1 + lv2 + lv3
      lv1 + lv2 + lv3 ~ sex + mig
      # specify covariances between latent variables
      lv1 ~~ lv2 + lv3
      lv2 ~~ lv3")
fit <- cfa(mod, data=dat, ordered = c("lv1_i01", "lv1_i02", "lv1_i03", "lv1_i04", "lv1_i05"), estimator = "WLSMV", missing="pairwise")
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

All the parameter estimates are fine, model fit is good.
The only thing is, I can't get rid off the following warning message:

Warning message:
In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble inverting W matrix; used generalized inverse

Any ideas on this issue are greatly appreciated.

Kind regards,
Ulrich
PS: Please find an example data set attachted.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: muthen1984 - problems with exogenous predictors
parts:
On 02/07/2017 06:13 PM, Ulrich Schroeders wrote:
> Dear Yves!
>
> Thanks, I also think so. Maybe you can give me some additional
> information on the error. It seems to occur with WLSMV estimator and
> exogenous (also dichotomous?) covariates.

I think it is related to this: when you create dummy latent variables
for sex.orig and mig.orig, lavaan will compute the joint correlation
matrix for all 'indicators', including sex.orig and mig.orig. But the
latter two are treated as continuous, while they are just binary.

Treating them as ordered (binary) seems to get rid of the warning,
although it triggers other identification issues.

That is all I have for now.

Yves.
